**Triage: lands in the Hono adapter / raw-mount path; `domain:cli`; `priority:p2`; class (b) against ADR-0112.**

A route mounted through `IHttpServer.getRawApp()` funnels through **neither** the adapter's `wrap()` **nor** any registrar wrapper ⇒ an escaped throw is answered by **Hono's own default handler**: `500 text/plain "Internal Server Error"`. **No ADR-0112 envelope, no `success` flag, no `code`** — and the thrown value's **own declared `status` / `code` are discarded**.

⇒ p2: a client parsing the platform's error envelope gets `text/plain` and cannot even read what failed. ⭐ And the discarded `status`/`code` is the sharper half: the throwing code **did** declare the right answer, and the transport threw it away — so the defect is invisible from the producer's side, which is where anyone would look.

⇒ Route raw mounts through the same envelope. ⚠️ **Establish what `getRawApp()` is for first** — if it exists precisely to bypass the adapter, then wrapping it silently defeats its purpose and the honest fix may be a documented refusal or an explicit opt-in. ⛔ Do not wrap it without saying what escape hatch remains.

⚠️ Correctly split out of #16545 at the `domain:cli` PM seat's explicit instruction ⇒ ⛔ do not fold back.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

## Zone 1 — RULING, and it comes with a named premise (⭐ read all three parts)

Triage left this open, verbatim: 「⚠️ **Establish what `getRawApp()` is for first** — if it exists precisely to bypass the adapter, then wrapping it silently defeats its purpose … ⛔ Do not wrap it without saying what escape hatch remains.」 **I have established it.** Here is the reading, then the ruling it rests on.

### The measurement that answers triage's question

The exemption `getRawApp()` carries is **scoped to route introspection, ⛔ not to the error envelope.** The contract says so in its own words — `packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts:290-295`, on **`getMountedRoutes()`**:

> - Routes an adapter mounts on its framework-native handle behind `getRawApp` are outside this table by construction, and so are `use` middleware and the `setFallbackHandler` seam: **this answers "what routes did I register", not "what paths might respond".**

And `:346-358` records *why* the member exists at all: four consumers were each declaring `getRawApp?(): any` locally, so it was hoisted into the contract — a **framework-handle accessor**, with `any` as the return type on purpose so the contract keeps no framework dependency.

⇒ ⭐ **Nothing in the contract exempts a raw mount from ADR-0112's refusal envelope.** Two different contracts: one about *what routes are listed*, one about *what a refusal looks like on the wire*. Conflating them is what makes "wrapping defeats its purpose" sound true when it is not.

### ① The ruling

**A door mounted on the platform's HTTP surface owes the declared ADR-0112 envelope on an escaped throw.** `500 text/plain "Internal Server Error"` with the thrown value's own declared `status`/`code` discarded is a contract violation, and it is fixed — ⛔ not documented as intended.

This is **pulling behaviour back to an already-declared contract**, which is why `Clause-②: no`: it widens no accept set and adds no public surface. ⇒ ⛔ Do **not** "fix" this by writing a doc that blesses the current answer.

### ② The premise this ruling hangs on — ⭐ verify it FIRST, and it is falsifiable

**Premise:** the `getRawApp()` escape hatch is about *framework-native mounting and ledger exemption*, and preserving it does **not** require preserving the non-envelope error answer. ⇒ an error seam on the raw handle (e.g. Hono's `onError` on the same app instance) leaves the hatch fully intact: consumers still mount natively, still stay outside `getMountedRoutes()`, still need no adapter verb.

⭐ **Verify this against the contract text yourself before you write code**, and say in the report which lines you read.

### ③ The prohibition — ⛔ no hard-doing, ⛔ no silent retreat

If you measure that the contract (or an ADR) **also** exempts raw mounts from the error envelope — i.e. the bypass is declared to cover error shape, not just route listing — then my premise is **false**. In that case:

⛔ **STOP. Report a fork.** ⛔ Do **not** wrap it anyway, and ⛔ do **not** silently fall back to "document the refusal instead". Either outcome is a product-contract decision that belongs to the maintainer, and I will file it to the decision box. A measured falsification here is a **good** outcome and counts as delivery, ⛔ not a failed round.

Say what you did. |
| 2 | no Hono `onError` handler exists on any app today | ✅ `git grep '\.onError('` over `packages/` returns only unrelated observability/pubsub callbacks — ⛔ zero on a Hono app |
| 3 | the fix is **one** place, not per-consumer | ⭐ my reading: the raw handle is one app instance, so one seam covers all 25 consumers. **Verify** — if raw consumers get *distinct* app instances, this assumption dies and the shape changes |
| 4 | `ValidationError` already maps specially on the wrapped path | ✅ `adapter.ts:234-235` — a bare `ValidationError` escaping a direct-mount handler answers `400`/`VALIDATION_FAILED`. ⇒ whatever you build must agree with the wrapped path, ⛔ not invent a second rule |

## Zone 3 — SUGGESTED ROUTE (optional; measurement outranks it)

Install an error seam on the raw Hono handle that funnels an escaped throw through the **same** `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` rule the wrapped path uses, so `/raw/*` and `/wrapped/*` answer the **same shape** for the same throw. The escape hatch survives: native mounting, ledger exemption, no adapter verb required.

## Acceptance — one named, independently checkable criterion

Re-run the card's own four-door matrix. `/raw/envelope` must answer **`503 application/json`** with `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",…}}` — i.e. the thrown value's declared `status`/`code` **honoured** — and `/raw/plain` must answer `500 application/json` with `INTERNAL_ERROR`. ⇒ the two raw doors must **stop being byte-identical**, which is precisely the reading that got this card split out of #16545.

⭐ **Minimum assertions on a refusal case are `code` + `status`** — ⛔ never "it didn't 200". Keep the wrapped pair in the same fixture as the lit control, so a green proves the raw path changed rather than proving the harness booted.

A changeset is owed unless `skip-changeset` genuinely applies.
